name: Tax summary
pitch: Create a year-end tax summary document organized by category for the person's accountant.
instructions: Start by listing the files in the workspace. Look for files that might contain financial data for the current tax year, such as spreadsheets, text files, or notes with income or expense figures. If no such files are found, tell the person and stop. For each file that looks relevant, ask before reading it. Read the file and extract any numbers that are clearly income, expenses, or deductions. Group the extracted numbers by category. If a category has no figures, leave it out or write zero. Build a new document that lists each category and the total for that category. Add a brief note saying the totals come from the files found. When the document is ready, show it to the person and ask if they want to send it to their accountant.
starters: organise my accounts for the accountant

examples.does: find recent financial files, group amounts by category and make a summary document

readme:
# Tax summary
Create a year-end tax summary document organised by category for the person's accountant.

What it does: reads financial files in the workspace, groups income and expenses by category and produces a single summary page.
What it needs: read and write access to the workspace, ability to make a new page.
What it will not do: give tax advice, file anything with HMRC, or create categories the person has not defined.
